full_judgment:
enlarged on bail in Druto Bichar Case No.06 of 2024 arising out of Moulavibazar Sadar Model Police Station Case No.12 dated 12-9-2024 corresponding to GR No.256 of 2024 (Moulavibazar Sadar) under sections 4 and 5 of the আইন শৃঙ্খলা বিঘ্নকারী অপরাধ (দ্রুত বিচার) আইন, ২০০২ (the Ain, 2002) now pending in the Court of Senior Judicial Magistrate and Druto Bichar Adalat, Moulavibazar and/or such other or further order or orders passed to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. Mr. Taimur Alam Khandaker, learned Advocate for the petitioners taking us through the materials on record submits that the allegation brought in the FIR against these petitioners do not come within the meaning of 'Aparadh' or 'Ain Sringkhala Bighnakari Apradh' as defined in section 2 of the Ain, 2002. The petitioners surrendered in this Court praying for anticipatory bail and in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.55129 of 2024 a Bench of this Division on 26-11-2024 passed order directing them to surrender before the Sessions Judge, Moulavibazar within 4 weeks from date. The petitioners complied with the said order and surrendered on 19-12-2024 as per direction with a prayer for bail but their prayer was rejected and they were sent to jail. Since then they are in jail. Moreover, other 2 co-accused Raku Kanti Nag and Sajal Chandra Das have been granted ad interim bail by this Bench in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 53602 and 55707 of 2024 respectively and they are enjoying its privilege. He adds that at the instance of another co-accused Rule has been issued and the proceeding of the aforesaid case has been stayed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.54731 of 2024 filed under section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to transfer the case from Moulavibazar district. The petitioners are in jail for more than 2 months. The offence is petty in nature. The trial of the case is uncertain and, as such, they are entitled to get bail in the aforesaid case. The Rule, therefore, would be made absolute. 

 5. Mr. Mohammad Asadur Rouf, learned Additional Attorney-General taking us through the contents of the FIR submits that the act done by these petitioners is direct affront to the judiciary. Accused-petitioner 1 by raising his hand in the Court room created anarchy and chaos. All the accused then abused the learned Judge as well as the staffs of the Court. At one stage they snatched away accused number 2 from the dock and took him outside the Court room. The acts of the accused definitely comes within the meaning of section 2(2), (q) and (w) of the Ain, 2002. Since the acts of the petitioners are direct threat and defamatory to the judiciary, they are not entitled to get bail in the aforesaid case. In the premises above, the Rule would be discharged. 

 6. The learned Deputy Attorney-General reported us today that the Rule issued in the miscellaneous case for transferring the case from Moulvibazar to any other district has been discharged on 23-2-2025. The opposite party State has already challenged interim bail granted to other 2 co-accused by this bench in the Appellate Division by filing leave petitions which are pending for hearing. 

 8. We have considered the submissions of both the sides and gone through the materials on record. It appears that in the FIR allegation has been brought against these petitioners and 4 others with 5/6 unknown accused of creating anarchy inside the Court room of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Moulavibazar. It has been alleged therein that all the accused including these petitioners used filthy languages towards the learned Judge, the Court staffs and other men present in the Court room and created anarchy. They snatched away petitioner number 2 from the dock and took him outside the Court room. The allegation brought against the petitioners undoubtedly undermines the prestige of the learned Judge which is alarming to the judiciary. At this stage we do not want to pass any remark or to decide whether the allegation brought against these petitioners comes within the definition of the aforesaid section of the Ain, 2002. It is to be decided in the trial of the case whether the petitioners are guilty of offence as alleged. The image, prestige and dignity of the judges and judiciary are to be protected by all of us but not only by the petty lawyers' clerk. But it is found that the case is pending in the Court of Druta Bichar Tribunal of Moulavibazar and the informant is a Bench Assistant of that Court. In fact the Court situated at Moulavibazar is a party to the proceeding. The petitioners reasonably apprehend that they will not get justice in dealing with bail application, if any, filed therein. At the end of the day it is found that sentence under the aforesaid sections is 2-7 years. The trial of the case is uncertain. In such a situation we being judges of this Court cannot fold our hands. We are, therefore, inclined to grant bail to the petitioners. Moreover, other 2 co-accused have been granted interim bail by this Bench on 26-11-2024 and 11-12-2024 in two separate miscellaneous cases and they are enjoying its privilege which are not yet stayed by the Appellate Division as reported by the learned Deputy Attorney-General. Moreover, the Rule issued at the instance of a co-accused in the miscellaneous case for transfer has been discharged by another Bench of this Division on 23-2-2025 which is found after the date of fixing this Rule for delivery of judgment on 18-2-2025. The co-accused has every scope to move to the appellate division against the aforesaid judgment. 

 9. In the premises above, we find merit in this Rule. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The accused-petitioners 1. Ranjit Kumar Nag alias Ranjit Kanti Nag, son of late Bidhu Bhushon Nag and 2. Jashobanta Bhatta-charjee, son of late Jagodindra Bhattacharjee be released on bail in the aforesaid case subject to the satisfaction of the Senior Judicial Magistrate and Druta Bichar Adalat, Moulavibazar.
